2308466.title: Union Education Minister releases Commemorative Publication on Bharat Innovates 2026
2308466.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Union Education Minister releases Commemorative Publication on Bharat Innovates 2026
Bharat Innovates connects young innovators with global opportunities, industry and networks: Shri Pralhad Joshi
Innovation, Research, Technology and Entrepreneurship are at the centre of India’s development journey: Union Education Minister
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today said that Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi consistently placed innovation, research, technology and entrepreneurship at the centre of India’s development journey. The Minister was speaking at the release of the Bharat Innovates 2026 Commemorative Publication in New Delhi, documenting the maiden edition of Bharat Innovates held in Nice, France, from 14 to 16 June 2026 under the aegis of the India-France Year of Innovation.

Shri Joshi said that Bharat Innovates reflected this vision of the Prime Minister by providing young innovators with opportunities to showcase their capabilities and connect with global stakeholders. Initiatives such as Bharat Innovates reflected the confidence and aspirations of young India and demonstrated the potential of the country’s higher education and research ecosystem. Bharat Innovates demonstrated what could be achieved when young talent was connected with opportunities, industry and global networks, he added.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, highlighted the important role of higher education institutions in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat. The National Education Policy 2020 accorded priority to research, innovation, creativity and scientific temper and initiatives such as Bharat Innovates provided a platform for translating these priorities into outcomes, the Minister added.

The Publication chronicles the journey of Bharat Innovates from the discovery and selection of promising deep-tech innovators from across the country to their international showcasing in Nice. It also captures the engagements, interactions and outcomes emerging from the initiative.

Bharat Innovates is an initiative of the Ministry of Education aimed at discovering and nurturing high-potential deep-tech innovations emerging from India’s higher education and research ecosystem. It seeks to connect innovators with industry, investors and other ecosystem stakeholders, accelerate technology translation and provide exposure to global markets and supply chains.

Bharat Innovates seeks to create a seamless pathway from laboratory to market and from campus to the world. The maiden edition brought together 120 deep-tech startups and innovators and 45 research projects from across India and provided them with opportunities to showcase their technologies, engage with industry and investors, and explore international collaborations and market opportunities.

The Commemorative Publication records this journey and highlights the scientific capability, entrepreneurial spirit and innovative potential of India’s students, researchers, faculty members, startups, higher education institutions and ecosystem partners.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood; Member, NITI Aayog, Prof. Abhay Karandikar; Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Ms. Deepti Gaur Mukerjee and senior officials of the Union Education Ministry were present at the Event held in a hybrid mode. Directors of IIT Kanpur, IIT Madras and IIT Bombay; senior academicians; representatives of the Department of Science and Technology, Department of Biotechnology, Department of Defence Production and IN-SPACe joined the programme online.

2308462.title: Global Community to Convene in New Delhi for Dryland Congress 2026; Over 800 Global Experts to Deliberate on Six Key Themes
2308462.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Global Community to Convene in New Delhi for Dryland Congress 2026; Over 800 Global Experts to Deliberate on Six Key Themes
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

The world’s scientific, policy and farming communities working on drylands will convene three-day Global Dryland Congress 2026, themed ‘Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South–South Cooperation’, in New Delhi from 10–12 September 2026.

Jointly organised by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT), the Congress will be held at the National Agricultural Science Complex and doubles as a milestone celebration of 50 years of ICAR–ICRISAT partnership.

The Congress arrives at a critical moment.  Drylands span about 45 percent of the world's land surface and are home to over two billion people, many of them smallholder farmers confronting climate variability, land degradation, water scarcity and shifting markets.

Over three days, more than 800 scientists, policymakers, farmer representatives and development partners from across Asia, Africa and the Americas will deliberate on six themes — breeding, climate resilience, nutrition and markets, farming systems, seed systems, and gender and youth inclusion — through panel discussions, keynote and lead presentations, parallel sessions and poster exhibitions.

The Congress will also commemorate the United Nations Day for South–South Cooperation on its final day, with a special ceremony and dedicated sessions on advancing South–South and Triangular Cooperation (SSTC) in agricultural research, convened jointly with CGIAR.

Proceedings will culminate in the adoption of the Delhi Declaration on Dryland (3D), along with the announcement of new partnerships, MOUs and awards recognising outstanding contributions to dryland science.

Union Minister of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will address the Congress as Chief Guest, alongside Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT; Ms Cathy Reade CRISAT Board Chair, Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General,ICAR; CGIAR Chief Scientist Dr Sandra Milach, former ICAR Director Generals Dr R.S. Paroda; Dr Panjab Singh, Dr T Mohapatra alongside Prof. S. G. Mohammed, Director,  Centre for Dryland Agriculture  Bayero University, Kano, Nigeria and former ICRISAT Director General Dr William Dar and other distinguished leaders, scientists and luminaries from across the globe advancing dryland agriculture.

2308447.title: Raksha Mantri calls on Sri Lankan Prime Minister in Colombo
2308447.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri calls on Sri Lankan Prime Minister in Colombo
Development cooperation figures prominently during the talks
India and Sri Lanka should continue to work on shared developmental vision for regional peace & prosperity and welfare of the people: Shri Rajnath Singh
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh called on the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka Dr Harini Amarasuriya in Colombo on September 09, 2026. The two leaders exchanged views on a range of issues, with development cooperation being one of the central themes of the discussions. They also reviewed progress in other areas of mutual interest including education, information technology, infrastructure, innovation and research. They also reflected upon the ancient civilisation ties and identified strong people-to-people exchanges as an ever-lasting  connection between the two nations.

Raksha Mantri underlined that as sister democracies with shared heritage, India and Sri Lanka should continue to work on a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region and welfare of their people. He underscored the importance of capacity building as one of the important pillars of cooperation. He conveyed that through this visit, he hopes to impart further momentum to the historic and multi-faceted India-Sri Lanka partnership.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that Prime Minister Amarasuriya is one of the role models for women not only in Sri Lanka but also in India, describing her as a symbol of women empowerment and Nari Shakti. He stated that India would like to encourage more women from Sri Lanka to benefit from the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) scholarships and other Government of India initiatives to increase their participation in governance and leadership. He added that there have been several strong women leaders in India and Sri Lanka who have contributed to nation-building.

2308444.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shri Bhagwat Prasad Makwana Assumes Charge as Chairperson of National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
Reaffirms Commitment to the Rights, Dignity and Socio-Economic Well-Being of Safai Karamcharis
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Bhagwat Prasad Makwana today assumed charge as the Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK). The Government of India appointed Shri Makwana to the post on 6 September 2026.

He has previously served as Vice-Chairman and Chairman of the Safai Karamchari Commission, Government of Uttarakhand. He has also served as an Independent Director on the Board of NHPC and as a Member of the Central Monitoring Committee constituted under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013.

Upon assuming charge, Shri Makwana reaffirmed his commitment to protecting the rights and dignity of Safai Karamcharis and advancing their socio-economic well-being. He also emphasised strengthening the Commission’s efforts towards their welfare and empowerment across the country.

Shri Makwana holds a Master’s degree in Economics and has extensive experience in social work, particularly in matters concerning the welfare and empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities.

2308442.title: From Rural Aspirations to GeoAI Excellence: Dr. Panchanan Das's Journey through Higher Education
2308442.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Rural Aspirations to GeoAI Excellence: Dr. Panchanan Das's Journey through Higher Education
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

Education and innovation can open new pathways for individuals with the determination to learn and excel. Timely fellowship assistance can provide scholars with the stability and resources required to pursue advanced research and translate their knowledge into meaningful professional achievement.

Demonstrating the impact of fellowship support, Dr. Panchanan Das, a 36-year-old scholar from the Scheduled Caste community, successfully completed his Ph.D. in Remote Sensing and GIS and built a career in geospatial technology. His journey reflects perseverance, continuous learning and the role of institutional support in enabling academic and professional advancement.

Dr. Das was raised in a rural family that valued education and hard work. His father worked as a daily wage labourer and supported the family's educational and household needs. Inspired by his family's resilience, Dr. Das remained focused on acquiring knowledge, developing specialised skills and creating better opportunities for his family.

During his academic journey, he had to manage the costs of higher education, research activities and technical resources. Delays in receiving fellowship payments during his Ph.D. added pressure and made it more difficult to maintain continuity in his studies and research work.

Growing up in a rural area also meant comparatively limited access to advanced educational facilities, professional exposure and modern technology. Opportunities for specialised training, career guidance and industry networks in emerging fields such as GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence and GeoAI were not readily available.

Despite these circumstances, Dr. Das remained committed to his goals. He continued to strengthen his capabilities through self-learning, research and sustained effort while balancing family responsibilities with the demands of higher education and professional development.

The scheme intervention provided financial, academic and fellowship support during his higher education and research. The assistance helped him continue his Ph.D., meet research-related requirements and enhance his technical skills in GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence, GeoAI and software engineering.

With the support received and his sustained dedication, Dr. Das successfully completed his Ph.D. in Remote Sensing and GIS. He is currently working with Uncharted AI as a Software Engineer and GeoAI Expert in Mapping and GIS, contributing to projects involving geospatial technologies, LiDAR and route optimisation.

His professional employment has enabled him to attain financial stability and support his family while continuing to grow in a specialised technology field. The transition from a rural academic environment to a career in GeoAI demonstrates how education and appropriate institutional assistance can expand professional opportunities.

Looking ahead, Dr. Das aspires to further develop his expertise in GeoAI and software engineering. He also aims to contribute to research and innovation through people-centric technological solutions in remote sensing, drone technology and geospatial analytics for wider public benefit.

Dr. Panchanan Das's journey highlights the transformative role of education, fellowship support and continuous skill development. His achievement stands as an inspiring example of ambition and perseverance strengthened by institutional support and professional opportunity.

2308431.body_html:

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Meets Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Commerce of Thailand Ms. Suphajee Suthumpun
India and Thailand Discuss Ways to Enhance Trade and Investment, Strengthen Business Linkages and Advance AITIGA Review
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal today met Ms. Suphajee Suthumpun, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Commerce of Thailand, at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi.

The two Ministers discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Thailand economic partnership, with a focus on enhancing bilateral trade and investment, expanding business opportunities and deepening business-to-business linkages between the two countries.

The two sides exchanged views on ways to further enhance trade and investment between India and Thailand through greater collaboration and co-creation of solutions in areas that can promote balanced and sustainable growth in bilateral trade. They also discussed strengthening trade promotion activities in both countries to foster business networks, facilitate greater business-to-business engagement and expand market opportunities for enterprises.

The two sides exchanged views on the progress of the review of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) and emphasised the need for deeper bilateral engagement through the India-Thailand Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in a time-bound manner.

Both sides recognised the importance of a balanced and mutually beneficial framework that can support greater market access and create opportunities for businesses in both countries.

The two Ministers also addressed a delegation of Thai businesses working across diverse areas, including space technologies, cold-chain logistics, food processing and innovation, health and wellness, and trade and investment promotion.

India and Thailand share longstanding civilisational, cultural and economic linkages, as well as a strategic partnership. The two countries have been working towards further expanding bilateral trade and investment and strengthening private-sector cooperation. Existing bilateral mechanisms have also emphasised the need to facilitate trade, resolve market-access issues and strengthen linkages with regional and global supply chains.

The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Thailand to further deepen economic engagement, strengthen business partnerships and build a robust, balanced and mutually beneficial trade and investment relationship.

2308398.title: UIDAI Launches Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK and Sandbox at Global Fintech Fest 2026
2308398.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
UIDAI Launches Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK and Sandbox at Global Fintech Fest 2026
Makes it easier for BFSI sector players to use Aadhaar face authentication for RBI-mandated multi-factor authentication
Users journey simplified: reduces the need for multiple apps for Aadhaar Face Authentication
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) on Wednesday launched the Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK (Software Development Kit) and Aadhaar Face Authentication Sandbox at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, enabling ecosystem partners to integrate, test and deploy Aadhaar Face Authentication more seamlessly within their digital applications.

The Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK brings UIDAI’s Face Authentication capability directly into native Android and iOS applications. It eliminates the need for users to switch between applications, enabling a smoother, single-app authentication experience.

The ready-to-use SDK simplifies integration for ecosystem partners while incorporating AI/ML-based liveness and anti-spoofing capabilities. It also supports secure handling and encryption of authentication data and is designed to work across consumer smartphones. The SDK is expected to help government departments, banks, fintechs and other organisations deploy Face Authentication-enabled services more efficiently.

Alongside the SDK, UIDAI also launched the Aadhaar Face Authentication Sandbox, a secure and controlled environment that allows organisations to integrate, test and validate the complete Face Authentication journey before production onboarding.

The Sandbox enables developers and quality assurance teams to test key stages, including user provisioning and consent, face capture, liveness checks, authentication, error handling, and response validation-- without requiring external biometric hardware. It also allows testing of failure scenarios such as invalid digital signatures, network interruptions, timeouts and spoofing attempts.

The launch of the SDK and Sandbox fulfills a long-standing demand of the Fintech and banking ecosystem to build a seamless, and secure user onboarding journey from within the user bank/fintech organisation’s mobile application.

It simplifies the journey. The user downloads only one app, say a banking/ insurance/  broking app and does Aadhaar authentication from within the app. Earlier, for a similar experience, a background app called FaceRD app was needed. This made the user onboarding journey longer and dependent on the presence of the Aadhaar FaceRD app.  With this launch, it reduces the need for multiple apps for Aadhaar Face Authentication

UIDAI’s indigenously engineered AI/ML-driven Face Authentication solution, which was launched in 2021, has processed over 500 crore transactions and been adopted by nearly 200 entities, including Union Government ministries and departments, State Governments, Banks, NBFCs, telecom operators, brokerage firms and certifying authorities among others. The technology received the Prime Minister’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration 2023 under the Innovation category.

Face Authentication is widely used across services like submission of Digital Life Certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) by pensioners, Ayushman Bharat beneficiary onboarding, DBT schemes, Aadhaar-enabled payments, SIM activation through e-KYC, beneficiary authentication for schemes like PM e-Drive, PM Awas Yojana and PM Kisan etc.

UIDAI also unveiled a “Playbook on ease of Onboarding” which will work as a guide for BFSI entities to get onboarded in the UIDAI authentication ecosystem for ID verification of its customers, staff, and other business partners.

2308395.title: Secure sea lanes and freedom of navigation are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of Indian Ocean Region, says Raksha Mantri at Sri Lankan Ministry of Defence
2308395.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Secure sea lanes and freedom of navigation are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of Indian Ocean Region, says Raksha Mantri at Sri Lankan Ministry of Defence
“India and Sri Lanka, as close maritime partners, are well positioned to jointly safeguard peace, security & stability across IOR”
“As true Vishwa Mitra, India is committed to playing a constructive and dependable role in its shared neighbourhood”
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

“Secure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region (IOR),” stated Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh as he called for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a favourable and secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests and brighter future. He was addressing a gathering comprising Sri Lankan Deputy Minister of Defence Mr Aruna Jayasekara, Commanders of the Sri Lankan Army, Navy & Air Force, and other senior officials during his visit to the country’s Ministry of Defence in Colombo on September 09, 2026.

Raksha Mantri asserted that national security and economic growth cannot be viewed in isolation as they are intrinsically linked to geography and security, emphasising that neither country can afford to remain indifferent to the developments in the region. He stated that while India and Sri Lanka have upgraded their capabilities through a series of measures ranging from capacity building to joint exercises, there is a need to further strengthen the longstanding  India-Sri Lanka defence and strategic partnership with special emphasis on maritime cooperation.

“We need to devise & implement joint protocols, sharpen the skills and share experiences to deal with emerging threats arising from the rapidly evolving global and regional dynamics. It needs to be a continuous process. We must develop new paradigms for a closer and stronger maritime partnership, which is the basis of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). ‘Mutual’ and ‘Holistic’ underscore the importance of synergy, cooperation and collaboration,” stated Shri Rajnath Singh.

Raksha Mantri stated that India and Sri Lanka are bound by the shared ocean, and maritime security is not a matter of abstract theory but a reality that shapes their trade, security and destinies. “Sri Lanka is a friendly neighbour, longstanding friend and reliable partner for India. Both nations are central to any strategic discourse on maritime security in the region. Strong India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation will be mutually beneficial and vital for collective growth and security,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the significant progress achieved in bilateral maritime cooperation, particularly in Search & Rescue Operations that have saved numerous precious lives at sea. He added that both nations have been working together in the fields of counter-narcotics, anti-piracy and human trafficking. “In this regard, our mutual association in Colombo Security Conclave which focuses on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, cyber security and organised crime becomes more relevant than ever before,” he said.

Raksha Mantri described the commissioning of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre, established through the collaboration between the two countries, as an excellent example of their shared commitment towards keeping the waters of the Indian Ocean safe and secure. “India stands ready to join hands with Sri Lanka in areas such as capacity building and joint exercises, enabling both sides to learn from each other’s experiences and fine-tune protocols for the effective implementation of joint initiatives. We’re committed to assisting Sri Lanka in every possible way to further strengthen such cooperation,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh envisaged a future where India and Sri Lanka emerge as joint stakeholders in developing a mutually beneficial and integrated Maritime Domain Awareness system, providing comprehensive maritime information on a real-time basis. “This would entail systematic cooperation and interaction amongst concerned agencies, navies and coast guards of the two countries with a view to addressing the challenges of illegal fishing, suspicious vessels tracking, narcotics trafficking, smuggling, terrorism and other security threats,” he said.

Referring to the challenges faced by our fishermen, Raksha Mantri underscored that the issue needs to be addressed together. He observed that maritime cooperation should extend beyond the security framework to also cover areas like aquaculture, marine biotechnology, ocean science, protection and preservation of maritime environment and maritime tourism. He also suggested that the two countries can explore the establishment of a joint Maritime Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) system involving relevant agencies for a coordinated and rapid response to natural calamities and man-made disasters.

Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that as the Indian Ocean enters a period of profound strategic and economic transformation, India and Sri Lanka must synergise their efforts, build upon their collective competencies and address emerging challenges together. “The tectonic shifts and rapid transformation underway present both challenges and opportunities. The two countries must leverage their longstanding maritime partnership to turn these opportunities into shared growth,” he said.

Raksha Mantri noted that the future of India-Sri Lanka relations should be anchored in the simple premise that proximity creates interdependence, which in turn creates immense opportunities for shared evolution. Describing India as a true Vishwa Mitra, or trusted global friend, he reiterated India’s commitment to playing a constructive and dependable role in its shared neighbourhood. Holistic maritime security and mutual prosperity are two sides of the same coin, he said. He expressed confidence that India and Sri Lanka, as close maritime partners, are well positioned to jointly safeguard peace, security and stability across the IOR.

High Commissioner of India to Sri Lanka Shri Santosh Jha and other senior officials were present on the occasion.

Upon his arrival at the Ministry of Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh was accorded a Guard of Honour. He also laid a wreath at the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) Memorial in Battaramulla and paid homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.

2308394.title: MSDE Organises ‘Skill Manthan’ on 'Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women'
2308394.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2308394.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE Organises ‘Skill Manthan’ on 'Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women'
Districts are the engines of economic growth and reform : Shri Jayant Chaudhary at the inaugural session of ‘Skill Manthan’
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised the inaugural session of ‘Skill Manthan’ centred on the theme ‘Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women’. The virtual dialogue highlighted innovative initiatives from Meerut and Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh and NTR District in Andhra Pradesh, demonstrating how district administrations can combine skilling, entrepreneurship, finance, technology, and market access to create sustainable livelihood opportunities for women. ‘Skill Manthan’ will serve as a knowledge-sharing platform to showcase innovative and impactful district-led initiatives.

Speaking on the initiative, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, said, “District administrations are the true engines of growth, reform and transformation. Through our district-led planning approach, we are ensuring that skilling initiatives are driven by local needs and aligned with the requirements of industry, particularly MSMEs. Supported by District Skill Development Plans, the skilling agenda is at the forefront of district administration, enabling more responsive, demand-driven and impactful outcomes for youth and local economies.”

Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “India’s skilling aspirations can only be realised when skill development is driven by local realities. Hyperlocal skilling, aligned to district needs and employment opportunities, is essential to equip our youth with relevant skills and connect them to meaningful livelihoods in a rapidly evolving economy.”

District Collectors and District Magistrates, Ms. Jasjit Kaur of Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, Dr. G. Lakshmisha of NTR, Andhra Pradesh and Dr. Vijay Kumar Singh of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh showcased innovative pathways for women’s economic empowerment through skilling, entrepreneurship, and market integration. Meerut demonstrated a women-centric manufacturing model that provides hands-on training and employment in badminton racket and shuttlecock production. Bijnor highlighted Vidur Prerna Swadeshi, a district-wide platform enabling rural women entrepreneurs through branding, market access, and enterprise support. NTR District’s RISE showcased a one-stop ecosystem offering skilling, credit facilitation, mentoring, employment linkages, and entrepreneurial support, illustrating how local institutions can be converged to create sustainable opportunities for women-led enterprises.

The session reaffirmed MSDE’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with district administrations and creating a national platform for documenting, sharing, and replicating successful grassroots models. Through Skill Manthan, district-level innovation will contribute to women’s economic participation, self-reliant communities, and the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

2308386.title: National Consumer Helpline facilitates refunds of over ₹105 crore to consumers in 15 months
2308386.ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
2308386.body_html:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
National Consumer Helpline facilitates refunds of over ₹105 crore to consumers in 15 months
1,66,189 refund-related grievances addressed across 35 sectors between 25 April 2025 and 31 July 2026
E-commerce sector accounts for more than ₹74 crore in facilitated refunds
Refunds ranging from ₹1 to ₹35.83 lakh facilitated in e-commerce sector during May-July 2026
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

The National Consumer Helpline (NCH), by the Department of Consumer Affairs, has facilitated refunds of more than ₹105 crore to consumers across 35 sectors by addressing 1,66,189 refund-related grievances during the fifteen-month period from 25 April 2025 to 31 July 2026.

The refunds were facilitated at the pre-litigation stage, enabling consumers to obtain timely relief without having to approach the Consumer Commissions. The National Consumer Helpline has emerged as a single-point access platform for consumers across the country to register grievances and seek resolution.

The e-commerce sector accounted for the largest share of refund-related grievances, with 1,00,466 complaints resulting in refunds of more than ₹74 crore. The Travel & Tourism sector followed, with refunds exceeding ₹10 crore. During May 2026 to July 2026, refunds facilitated in the e-commerce sector ranged from ₹1 to ₹35,83,790, covering consumer grievances of varying nature and value.

Key highlights:

  • ₹105 crore+ refunds facilitated
  • 1,66,189 refund-related grievances addressed
  • 35 sectors covered
  • 1,00,466 e-commerce refund grievances addressed
  • ₹74 crore+ refunds facilitated in the e-commerce sector
  • ₹10 crore+ refunds facilitated in Travel & Tourism
  • ₹1 to ₹35,83,790 – range of refunds facilitated in e-commerce during May-July 2026

The NCH operates through a convergence-based mechanism under which consumer grievances are digitally forwarded to the concerned companies for resolution within defined timelines. The process is supported by continuous monitoring and tracking of consumer feedback.

Refund-related grievances received through NCH have come from metropolitan cities as well as remote regions across the country, reflecting the platform's reach as a pan-India mechanism for consumer grievance redressal.

Consumer grievances resolved through NCH

  • Bengaluru Urban | Delayed mobile phone delivery: A consumer who ordered a mobile phone worth ₹47,490 on 21 August 2026, with delivery scheduled for 22 August, approached NCH after repeated extensions of the delivery date. Following NCH intervention, the e-commerce platform processed a full refund of ₹47,490.

 

  • NTR District, Andhra Pradesh | Incorrect product received: A consumer received a USB 3.1 enclosure instead of the ordered 2.5-inch Hard Drive Enclosure, USB-C 3.0 to Type-C, which was incompatible with the required device. Following registration of the grievance with NCH, the e-commerce platform processed a refund for the product.

 

  • Udalguri, Assam | Two-wheeler booking refund: A consumer approached NCH on 21 May 2026 following cancellation of a two-wheeler booking and delay in refunding the ₹5,000 booking amount. Following intervention, the dealer processed the refund of the booking amount and confirmed its credit to the consumer's account.

 

  • Poonch, Jammu & Kashmir | Wrong and substandard product: A consumer who ordered sports shoes worth ₹3,072 received a different and substandard brand. After repeated cancellation/rejection of the return request, the consumer registered a grievance with NCH on 29 June 2026. Following intervention, the e-commerce platform processed a refund for the product.

NCH provides multiple channels for consumer access

The National Consumer Helpline provides consumers access to grievance redressal in 17 languages through multiple channels:

  • Toll-free: 1915
  • WhatsApp/SMS: 8800001915
  • INGRAM Portal
  • Email: nch-ca[at]gov[dot]in
  • NCH Mobile App
  • Web Portal
  • UMANG App

The facilitation of refunds exceeding ₹105 crore during the period from 25 April 2025 to 31 July 2026 highlights the role of NCH in providing accessible and time-bound grievance redressal at the pre-litigation stage.

The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) under the Department of Consumer Affairs is strengthening consumer protection by ensuring timely grievance redressal at the pre-litigation stage. From 25 April 2025 to 31 July 2026, NCH facilitated ₹105 crore+ in refunds while resolving… pic.twitter.com/ZfT8xhXRir

— Pralhad Joshi (@JoshiPralhad) September 9, 2026

The initiative also contributes to strengthening consumer confidence in digital marketplaces and service ecosystems by providing consumers with a convenient mechanism to raise grievances and seek timely resolution. Consumers are encouraged to proactively utilise the National Consumer Helpline to safeguard their consumer rights and seek redressal of their grievances.

MoS for Railways Shri V. Somanna Reviews Safety, Operations, Punctuality and Public Grievances at Delhi Division Control Office
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for Railways & Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna today visited the Control Office of Delhi Division and reviewed various aspects of railway operations, including safety, train operations, punctuality and public grievances. During the visit, the Minister interacted with officials and staff of the Control Office. He also held detailed discussions with DRM Delhi Shri Pushpesh R. Tripathi and his team.

The Control Office serves as the nerve centre of a Railway Division, where train running, maintenance planning, supervision and safety-related activities are monitored round the clock. These functions are carried out 24 hours a day, seven days a week and 365 days a year.

Minister Reviews Functioning of Key Control Verticals

During the visit, Shri V. Somanna observed the functioning of Section Controllers and various other verticals of the Control Office, including Engineering, Coaching, Goods, Commercial, Signal & Telecom, Traction and Security Controls. He also visited the state-of-the-art Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Centre and the War Room of Delhi Division.

Delhi Division is among the most complex administrative divisions of the Indian Railways network. During his interaction with officials and staff, the Minister understood the complexities of railway operations and gained insights from frontline staff to identify areas for further improvement.

The discussions covered opportunities for greater technology adoption, improvement in staff working conditions and future development of railway operations and infrastructure.

Technology Adoption Strengthening Railway Safety and Operations

Shri V. Somanna highlighted the rapid adoption of technology across various aspects of railway working, including train operations, safety supervision and maintenance monitoring. He noted that under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, technology adoption in Indian Railways has accelerated significantly across these areas.

Technology-enabled systems have helped reduce human errors and enhance safety and these efforts will be further strengthened in the future with continued focus on Make in India and other policy initiatives, Shri V. Somanna mentioned.

Shri Somanna appreciated the discipline, dedication and hard work of Railway staff, noting that Railway employees work round the clock with a level of commitment comparable to that of the Army.

The visit reaffirmed the importance of strengthening technology-driven monitoring, operational efficiency, safety supervision and staff-centric improvements to further enhance the performance of Indian Railways.

2308382.title: Spiritual Strength for a Drug-Free India
2308382.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Spiritual Strength for a Drug-Free India
Four More Spiritual Organisations Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Chinmaya Mission, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan and Hare Krishna Movement Join Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan; Sign MoUs with Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment in Presence of Secretary Sudhansh Pant
Partnerships to Strengthen Grassroots Awareness, Prevention, Recovery and Social Mobilization against Substance Abuse
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

As part of strengthening its efforts towards building a Nasha Mukt Bharat, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with four prominent spiritual organizations namely Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Chinmaya Mission, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan and Hare Krishna Movement, at the Ministry’s Chintan Conference Hall in the National Capital here today.

The MoUs were signed in presence of Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Dr. Sandeep R. Rathod, Joint Secretary (Drug Prevention); senior officials of the Department; and representatives of the participating spiritual organizations.

Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Director (Drug Prevention), signed the MoUs on behalf of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. The MoUs were exchanged amid applause from the participants.

The respective organisations were represented by Shri Chandra Singh, Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra; Smt. Prema Vishwanath, Chinmaya Mission; Sadhvi Shitabha Bharti, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan; and Shri Fateh Chand Sharma, Hare Krishna Movement, who signed the MoUs on behalf of their organisations.

The partnerships form part of the Department's continuing efforts under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to leverage the extensive reach, influence and community networks of spiritual and value-based organisations for strengthening awareness, prevention and social mobilization against substance abuse.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, reiterated the importance of spiritual organizations in advancing the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat. He appreciated the efforts of the organizations already associated with the Ministry and noted that their collective initiatives under NMBA have helped the Department reach more than 34.42 crore citizens.

The Secretary called upon the newly partnered organizations to maximize their outreach and utilize their extensive networks to spread the message of prevention, awareness and recovery from substance abuse, particularly at the grassroots level. He emphasized that the collective strength of the Government, civil society and spiritual organizations could help create a sustained social movement against drug abuse.

Shri Pant said that the participation of spiritual organisations under NMBA seeks to bring together spiritual strength, social responsibility and community mobilization. He said their extensive grassroots presence can play a significant role in fostering resilience among individuals and families, reducing the stigma associated with substance use disorders, and encouraging affected persons to seek timely help, treatment and rehabilitation.

The Secretary further said that through these partnerships, the Ministry aims to ensure that the message of prevention, recovery, compassion and social responsibility reaches diverse sections of society and develops into a sustained people's movement.

Shri Pant added that the expanding network of spiritual and social organizations will further reinforce the collective resolve to realize the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat.

The Secretary noted that these partnerships have contributed significantly to mass awareness, volunteer mobilization and the integration of yoga, meditation, spiritual counselling and value-based approaches into initiatives aimed at preventing substance abuse and supporting recovery.

Pertinently, the Ministry has previously entered into MoUs with The Art of Living, Brahma Kumaris, Sant Nirankari Mission, ISKCON, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, All World Gayatri Pariwar, Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Dhanwantari Ashram and the University of Patanjali, as part of recognizing the important role played by spiritual organizations in guiding communities, instilling discipline, promoting value-based living and strengthening individual and family resilience.

As part of the programme, an Anti-Drug Pledge was administered by the Secretary to the representatives of the participating organizations. The organisations were also urged to administer the pledge during their major programmes, events and public gatherings to reinforce the collective commitment towards building a drug-free society.

The three short films produced by the Ministry highlighting the importance of awareness about ill effects of substance abuse besides rehabilitation of the victims of drug abuse, were screened on the occasion. In addition, the participants were informed about the initiatives like registration as Nasha Mukti Mitra and taking E-Pledge, on the NMBA portal.

2308345.title: Union Health Ministry Organises National Multi-Stakeholder Workshop on Fluorosis on National Fluorosis Day
2308345.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2308345.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Organises National Multi-Stakeholder Workshop on Fluorosis on National Fluorosis Day
Workshop Brings Together Key Stakeholders to Strengthen NPPCF through Research, Innovation and Multisectoral Action
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, through the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), organised a National Multi-Stakeholder Workshop on ‘Fluorosis’ on the occasion of National Fluorosis Day, bringing together key stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening prevention, early detection, management and control of fluorosis under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF).

The workshop brought together representatives from the Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), AIIMS, National Dental Commission (NDC), State Nodal Officers and Consultants, among other stakeholders. The participation of institutions and experts from diverse sectors underscored the need for a coordinated and multisectoral approach to addressing fluorosis.

The workshop focused on expanding the reach and coverage of NPPCF, strengthening programme implementation through research and innovation, and promoting multisectoral action for effective prevention and control of fluorosis.

Addressing the Inaugural Session, Dr. Puspa Lata, Addl. DG, DGHS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provided an overview of the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF) and its objectives towards prevention, early detection and management of fluorosis. She also underscored the importance of strong multi-sectoral coordination and real-time information sharing to strengthen fluorosis prevention and control efforts.

Speaking at the Occasion, Shri Lalit Wadhwa, Joint Secretary, Ministry of the Health and Family Welfare, highlighted the importance of inter-sectoral convergence, particularly with sectors dealing with drinking water and sanitation, given the close link between excessive fluoride exposure and the occurrence of fluorosis.

The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF) aims to prevent and control fluorosis through surveillance, capacity building, health education, early diagnosis and management of cases, along with appropriate inter-sectoral interventions to address excessive fluoride exposure.

The multi-stakeholder platform also facilitated the sharing of experiences, best practices and field-level learnings among States/UTs and other stakeholders, with the objective of further strengthening programme implementation and ensuring effective prevention and control of fluorosis.

The workshop reaffirmed the commitment of the Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare towards strengthening public health interventions for fluorosis and promoting awareness, early detection and access to appropriate care, thereby contributing to healthier communities and improved quality of life.

2308335.title: Crackdown on Fake Seeds: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to Hold Nationwide Consultation with Farmer Leaders on September 10
2308335.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Crackdown on Fake Seeds: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to Hold Nationwide Consultation with Farmer Leaders on September 10
Tougher Seed Law in the Works: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to Hear Farmers’ Voices Before Finalising New Seed Bill
No More Compromise on Seed Quality: Centre Plans Tough New Law; Shri Shivraj to Engage Farmer Leaders on September 10
From Kashmir to Kanyakumari, Farmers to Have Their Say on New Seed Law as Shri Shivraj Leads Key Consultation
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is preparing to introduce a new and stringent Seed Act aimed at protecting the country’s farmers from the losses caused by fake and substandard seeds. The proposed legislation is part of the Modi government’s efforts to realise Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a prosperous and self-reliant farming community. Before finalising the proposed legislation, Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will hold a high-level consultation with senior leaders of major farmer organisations from across the country on September 10 at 4:00 PM at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi.

The consultation, convened by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, is aimed at incorporating farmers’ ground-level experiences, suggestions and concerns directly into the draft seed legislation. The government intends to build a robust and effective regulatory framework to curb the activities of seed mafias and protect farmers from fraudulent and poor-quality seeds.

The proposed new Seed Act is expected to provide for stringent legal action against companies and traders involved in the sale of fake, adulterated or substandard seeds, including heavy penalties and imprisonment. Poor-quality seeds can wipe out months of a farmer’s hard-earned income and years of effort and labour. The government’s stated position is that the new law must ensure the highest standards of seed quality and a transparent, end-to-end traceability system, while also safeguarding farmers’ rights over traditional seeds.

The consultation on September 10 will bring farmer representatives together from across the country. Senior leadership of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, various factions of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU), All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC), Kisan Mahapanchayat, Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Gaon Kisan Unnayan and the Society for Independent Farmers Association (SIFA) will participate in the meeting.

Ground-level farmer representatives from several states will also put forward their views before the Union Agriculture Minister. These include representatives of the Karnataka Raitha Sangha, Telangana Raitha Sangha, Maharashtra’s Shetkari Organisation, Gujarat’s Khedut Samaj, the National Kisan Progressive Association from Rajasthan and Bihar, Tamil Nadu’s Vivasayigal Sangam, Jharkhand’s Pragatisheel Krishi Manch, and a farmers’ organisation from Kottayam in Kerala, among others.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has emphasised that, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the government is committed to framing policies through dialogue and consensus with farmers.

The consultation, being held ahead of the upcoming Parliament session, is expected to mark a significant step towards creating a stronger regulatory framework and protecting Indian agriculture from the persistent threat of fake and substandard seeds.

2308334.title: Self-assembly of organic molecules opens a new path to green hydrogen production
2308334.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Self-assembly of organic molecules opens a new path to green hydrogen production
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi

A simple yet powerful strategy of integrating naturally occurring amino acid with a light-absorbing organic molecule could improve solar driven hydrogen production using completely metal free organic materials. 

Hydrogen is considered one of the most promising clean energy carriers because its combustion produces only water, making it an environmentally benign alternative to fossil fuels. One of the promising methods for producing green hydrogen is by using sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. However, most existing photocatalysts rely on inorganic semiconductors or precious metals, which are often expensive, difficult to manufacture, and raise concerns regarding long-term sustainability. Developing efficient metal-free organic photocatalysts has therefore remained a major scientific challenge.

A team of researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, -an autonomous institute under Department of Science and Technology (DST), integrated a naturally occurring amino acid (aspartic acid) with a light-absorbing organic molecule, perylene diimide (PDI) and allowed the molecules to spontaneously organize themselves through supramolecular self-assembly.

They found that the enhanced performance arises from how the molecule organizes itself. The amino acid moiety promotes strong, extended hydrogen bonding, while the PDI chromophore drives π–π stacking and efficient light absorption.

Thus, the synergistic interplay between the two governs the molecular organization and, consequently, the functional properties of the material.

The researchers synthesised an aspartic acid-functionalized perylene diimide (PDI) molecule that spontaneously self-assembled in water into highly ordered two-dimensional nanosheets.

This subtle molecular reorganization dramatically broadened light absorption, enhanced charge separation, reduced energy losses, and increased the accessible surface area for catalytic reactions without altering the molecule's chemical composition. As a result, the self-assembled material generated nearly 18% higher photocurrent than its bulk counterpart during solar-driven water splitting.

Advanced electrochemical measurements together with density functional theory (DFT)

calculations further revealed that self-assembly promotes more efficient charge transport, while the amino acid increases the molecular dipole moment, facilitating effective separation of photo-generated charges that drive hydrogen evolution.

The study further demonstrates that naturally occurring amino acids can serve not only as molecular building blocks but also as powerful regulators of supramolecular organization and photocatalytic performance. This molecular design strategy offers a sustainable route to developing efficient, environmentally friendly, and metal-free photocatalysts for solar energy conversion.

The work led by Dr. Goutam Ghosh and Dr. Ashutosh K. Singh at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, together with Mr. Sourav Moyra, Mr. Kumar Shubham, and Ms. Athira Chandran M was published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, one of the Royal Society of Chemistry's leading journals.

Such materials could contribute to future technologies for green hydrogen production, artificial photosynthesis, solar fuel generation, and next-generation renewable energy devices, reducing dependence on costly and scarce metals.

Publication Link: https://doi.org/10.1039/d6ta04378j

2308326.title: Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu Calls on Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh; Discussions Focus on Weather Early-Warning, Lavender Cultivation and Astro-Tourism
2308326.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2308326.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu Calls on Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh; Discussions Focus on Weather Early-Warning, Lavender Cultivation and Astro-Tourism
CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu appreciates support of Modi Government for five Doppler Weather Radars and further strengthening weather early-warning system in Himachal Pradesh
In Himachal, Aroma Mission has extended lavender cultivation to Upper Bhamla, Tehsil Baldwara, district Mandi; Dr Jitendra Singh Discusses its further Expansion
Possibility of High-Altitude Sky Observatory in Spiti Explored for Science, Students and Astro-Tourism discussed
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in New Delhi today and discussed a range of issues concerning the State, including strengthening weather observation and early-warning systems, expansion of lavender cultivation under the CSIR Aroma Mission, grassroots-level weather forecasting, the possibility of a high-altitude sky observatory in Spiti, and issues related to the Himachal Pradesh State cadre.

During the meeting, the Chief Minister appreciated and thanked the Government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for five Doppler Weather Radars support for Himachal Pradesh, while discussing the need to further strengthen the State's weather observation and early-warning capabilities. Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed that necessary steps should be taken to ensure that Himachal Pradesh has an adequate early-warning system, particularly keeping in view its difficult mountainous terrain and vulnerability to extreme weather events. The meeting also covered the proposed expansion of the weather observation network in the State.

Chief Secretary of Himachal Pradesh Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant and senior officials were also present during the meeting.

Himachal Pradesh currently has three Doppler Weather Radars, at Kufri, Jot and Murari Devi, while two more are in the pipeline, making the total five. The proposed expansion includes two additional Doppler Weather Radars, one in Lahaul-Spiti and another in Kinnaur.

The existing IMD observational network in the State also includes 28 Automatic Weather Stations, 64 Automatic Rain Gauges and 84 Daily Rainfall Monitoring Stations.

The proposed expansion also includes 20 Automatic Weather Stations, 24 Automatic Rain Gauges, 21 Automatic Snow Gauges and one Radio Sonde/Radio Wind system. Suitable sites for the proposed radars in Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur are currently being examined, with site selection facing technical issues related to beam blockage.

The discussions also covered the Gram Panchayat-level weather forecast being provided by the India Meteorological Department, aimed at taking location-specific weather information closer to people at the grassroots. The service, known as Mausamgram, provides weather forecasts at Gram Panchayat level and is designed to make localised weather information available for everyday decision-making, including for farmers.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also discussed the expansion of the successful lavender cultivation model under the CSIR Aroma Mission in Himachal Pradesh. Under Phase III of the CSIR Aroma Mission, CSIR-IIIM Jammu has extended lavender cultivation to Upper Bhamla, Tehsil Baldwara, District Mandi, where 20,000 lavender cuttings have been planted and around 150 farmers have been associated with the initiative. The initial trials have been successful, and more area is proposed to be brought under lavender cultivation this season. Distillation units are also proposed to be provided to farmers under Phase IV of the Aroma Mission.

The Minister also referred to the expansion of the lavender initiative beyond Jammu & Kashmir, including Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Arunachal Pradesh, with the model seeking to connect cultivation with industry and value addition so that farmers can derive greater livelihood benefits from the crop.

Another key issue discussed was the possibility of establishing a high-altitude sky observatory in Spiti. The proposal is being explored in consultation with the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, taking advantage of the region's high-altitude location and favourable conditions for astronomical observations. The proposed concept envisages a scientific facility that can also support students and educational activities, while opening up opportunities for astro-tourism and stargazing.

The discussions included the possibility of combining a telescope facility for scientific studies and use by college students with smaller telescope-based facilities that could enable tourists to experience stargazing. A detailed proposal from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics is expected to take the initiative forward.

The meeting also covered issues related to the Himachal Pradesh State cadre, including matters arising from the cadre review process. The discussions were confined to the issues concerning the State and the appropriate procedural course of action, without indicating any final decision on cadre strength or restructuring.

The discussions reflected the potential of science and technology interventions to address some of Himachal Pradesh's distinctive challenges—from timely weather warnings in its vulnerable mountain regions and technology-led livelihood opportunities for farmers, to scientific exploration and new tourism opportunities in high-altitude areas.

2308264.title: Cabinet approves five multitracking projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms
2308264.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Cabinet approves five multitracking projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms
The total estimated cost of the projects is Rs. 10,021 crore and planned to be completed up to 2029-30
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved five projects of Ministry of Railways with total cost of Rs. 10,021 crore (approx.). These projects include:

  1. Arakkonam – Renigunta 3rd and 4th Line – 77 kms
  2. Whitefield – Bangarapet 3rd and 4th Line – 47 kms
  3. Hosur – Omalur Doubling – 147 kms
  4. Salem – Karur – Dindigul Doubling – 159 kms
  5. Multitracking of Secunderabad (Ghatkesar) – Kazipet – 110 kms

The increased line capacity will significantly enhance mobility, resulting in improved operational efficiency and service reliability for Indian Railways. These multi-tracking projects are poised to streamline operations and alleviate congestion. The projects are in line with the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Vision of a New India which will make people of the region “Atmanirbhar” by way of comprehensive development in the area which will enhance their employment/ self-employment opportunities.

The projects are planned on PM-Gati Shakti National Master Plan with focus on enhancing multi-modal connectivity and logistic efficiency through integrated planning and stakeholder consultations. These projects will provide seamless connectivity for movement of people, goods, and services.

The five projects covering 17 Districts across the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, will increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 Kms. The approved multi-tracking projects will enhance connectivity to approx. 2,121 villages, which are having a population of about 52 lakhs.

The approved capacity enhancement will improve rail connectivity to several prominent tourist destinations across the country, including Tirupati, Subramaniya Swamy Temple (Tiruttani), Sri Padmavati Ammavaari Temple (Tiruchanur), Kotilingeshwara Devaalaya, Sri Seethi Byraveshwara Swamy Temple, Bangaru Tirupati, Kolar Gold Fields, Hogennakkal Falls, Hosur Fort, Mettur Dam, Kodaikanal Hills, Sathyamangalam Wildlife Sanctuary, Namakkal Anjaneyar Temple, Namakkal Fort, Kalyana Pasupatheswar Temple, Yadagirigutta Temple, Bhongir Fort, Surendrapuri, Swarnagiri Temple, etc.

These projects are essential routes for transportation of commodities such as coal, cement, iron and steel, container, automobile, food grains, petroleum products, fertilizers, etc. The capacity augmentation works will result in additional freight traffic of magnitude 47 MTPA (Million Tonnes Per Annum). The Railways being environment friendly and energy efficient mode of transportation, will help both in achieving climate goals and minimizing logistics cost of the country, reduce oil import (~8 crore Litres) and lower CO2 emissions (~42 crore Kg) which is equivalent to plantation of ~2 crore trees.

2308213.title: Raksha Mantri pays a courtesy call on Sri Lankan President in Colombo
2308213.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri pays a courtesy call on Sri Lankan President in Colombo
India and Sri Lanka reaffirm commitment to shared progress & people welfare while ensuring regional security and prosperity
As closest friend and neighbour, India considers it a responsibility to provide assistance as first responder, will continue to do so: Shri Rajnath Singh
Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India’s security interests: Mr Anura Kumara Dissanayake
Both sides ink MoUs on upgradation of L70 Guns for Sri Lankan Air Force and cooperation between National Cadet Corps & National Defence Colleges of the two countries
Three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces virtually inaugurated
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh called on the President of Sri Lanka Mr Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo on September 09, 2026. The two leaders held substantive discussions on issues covering the entire spectrum of the multi-faceted partnership between the two nations, characterised by traditionally warm relations and mutual trust.

The two sides reaffirmed that as civilisational twins, close neighbours & maritime partners, India and Sri Lanka would continue to work together for their development & welfare of the people while working jointly to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region. Raksha Mantri conveyed greetings on behalf of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical & civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges.

Extending a warm welcome to Raksha Mantri, President Dissanayake recalled his interactions with PM Modi and reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for any activities inimical to India’s security interests. 

President Dissanayake expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Operation Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New Delhi to facilitate reconstruction and rehabilitation work across different parts of the island. Raksha Mantri emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, India considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as well.

Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces. The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 Guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between National Cadet Corps (NCC) & National Defence Colleges (NDC) of both the countries. The MoU on Upgradation of six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force falls under a Government of India grant. The upgradation of these air defence guns will significantly strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka. These air defence guns were earlier provided to the Sri Lanka Air Force by India.

The MoU on academic cooperation between NDC, India and NDC, Sri Lanka will facilitate knowledge sharing which will be a significant step in further strengthening the academic bonds between both the sister institutes. The MoU on NCC cooperation will formalise the NCC youth exchange programme between India and Sri Lanka. This exchange programme provides a valuable opportunity for NCC cadets from multiple countries across the world to come to New Delhi every year and participate in NCC events.

2308205.title: MC²+ to Launch Dedicated Co-working Space and Innovation Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati Tomorrow
2308205.body_html:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
MC²+ to Launch Dedicated Co-working Space and Innovation Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati Tomorrow
New facility to offer 50+ workstations, 16 cabins, investor and technical consultant rooms to boost startup ecosystem in the Northeast
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi

MC²+ will tomorrow launch a dedicated Node and Co-working Space on the 6th Floor of the NRL Centre, Guwahati, marking a significant step in its efforts to strengthen India's startup and innovation ecosystem, with particular focus on the Northeast.

Located in the heart of Guwahati, the new facility has been envisioned as a vibrant, collaborative and professionally equipped environment for startups, entrepreneurs and innovators. Designed around the evolving needs of emerging ventures, it brings together best-in-class infrastructure, professional support, technical expertise, investor access and industry connections under one roof.

The facility offers 50+ dedicated workstations, 16 cabins, 4 investor meeting rooms and 2 technical consultant rooms, along with 2 meeting rooms, a full-fledged cafeteria and common areas. The infrastructure has been designed and developed as a best-in-class facility, benchmarked against leading startup and innovation spaces nationally, giving startups a professional and contemporary environment to work, collaborate and grow.

The investor rooms will provide dedicated spaces for founders to present their ideas, engage with potential investors and explore opportunities for funding and strategic partnerships. The technical consultant rooms will facilitate focused interactions with experts, enabling startups to seek guidance on technology development, product refinement and technical challenges.

The value of the space extends well beyond its physical infrastructure. MC²+ will provide startups with access to a comprehensive support ecosystem comprising domain experts, technical consultants, legal advisors, and specialised finance and audit consultants — enabling entrepreneurs to seek professional guidance across critical areas such as technology and product development, intellectual property, contracts and regulatory requirements, financial planning, accounting, audit preparedness, compliance and business structuring.

Beyond the formal workspaces, a full-fledged cafeteria and café pantry have been designed to encourage informal interactions and networking, providing an environment where entrepreneurs can take a break, exchange ideas and build connections that can evolve into meaningful collaborations.

The vision behind the initiative is to create an environment where startups can access much more than a place to work — a platform where they can find the infrastructure, expertise, mentorship, professional guidance and connections required at different stages of their journey.

The establishment of the MC²+ Node at NRL Centre, Guwahati, marks an important step towards strengthening the startup and innovation ecosystem in Guwahati and the Northeast. It aims to bring together entrepreneurs, experts, investors and industry stakeholders, creating an environment where ideas can move from conception to development, validation and scale.

The formal inauguration will take place tomorrow, September 10, 2026, at the NRL Centre, Guwahati.

2308195.title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses Special Session of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly
2308195.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses Special Session of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly
‘Rashtra Pratham’ and ‘Viksit Bharat @ 2047’ Must Guide Legislative Work: Vice-President
‘Debates, Discussions or Even Disruptions Must Lead to a Decision’: Vice President
Arunachal Pradesh’s Progress Is Integral to India’s Development and Security: Vice-President
Responsible Utilisation of Arunachal Pradesh’s Hydropower Potential Can Boost State Revenue and Development: Vice-President
Posted On: 09 SEP 2026 1:46PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar, calling upon legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation.

 

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Special Session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Itanagar today, and called upon the legislators to uphold the highest traditions of democracy and work towards the development of the State and the nation.

The… pic.twitter.com/DqaslGe58V

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 9, 2026


On his arrival at the Assembly premises, the Vice-President paid floral tributes to the statues of Mahatma Gandhi and Babasaheb Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour. He also visited the Arunachal Pradesh Assembly Museum, which showcases the evolution and growth of the State Legislature and its legislative journey.

Addressing the Assembly, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Arunachal Pradesh has immense strategic importance, rich cultural heritage and abundant natural resources, and plays a vital role in safeguarding the nation’s borders. He noted that the security of the rest of the country is closely linked to the protection of the borders by the people of Arunachal Pradesh.

Emphasising India’s unity amid its diversity, the Vice-President said that the country is united by one Constitution, one vision of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First) and one goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Quoting national poet Subramania Bharati, he highlighted the unity of thought underlying India’s diverse languages and traditions.

Recalling India’s rich democratic heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan described India as the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and urged legislators to live up to this legacy.

The Vice-President highlighted the growing focus on the development of the North-East, recalling the establishment of the Ministry of DoNER during the tenure of former Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee and the emphasis on the region under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Act East Policy. He congratulated the Government and people of Arunachal Pradesh for the State’s development achievements, including its emergence as the country’s leading producer of kiwi, expansion of road infrastructure, issuance of over one lakh Soil Health Cards and significant progress in education and per capita income.

Congratulating the State Legislature on completing its Golden Jubilee, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated initiatives such as making the Legislative Secretariat plastic-free and establishing the Assembly Library and Museum.

Urging legislators to place public service above electoral success, the Vice-President said that elections may be won through votes, but the respect and trust of people can only be earned through dedicated service. He called upon Members to make effective use of Question Hour and Zero Hour to raise issues concerning public policy and their constituencies.

As the Presiding Officer of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised the importance of dialogue, debate and discussion in legislative functioning. Reiterating his message that “debates, discussions, or even disruptions must always lead to a decision,” he said that healthy debate strengthens democracy and constructive cooperation advances the State and the nation.

The Vice-President said that there can be no Viksit Bharat without a Viksit Arunachal Pradesh, stressing that development must be inclusive and no tribal or marginalised community should be left behind. He also emphasised the need to balance environmental concerns with responsible utilisation of natural resources for the economic development and welfare of the people. Referring to Arunachal Pradesh’s significant hydropower potential, he said its appropriate utilisation could generate greater revenue and accelerate the State’s development.

Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik, Speaker of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly Shri Tesam Pongte, Chief Minister Shri Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Members of the Legislative Assembly, senior officials of the State Government and Legislative Secretariat were present on the occasion.
